Simulated mortality data with known truth

Source: R/data-example.R
mt_example.Rd

Generates a two-stratum dataset (women and men) from a Lee-Carter-type model with Gompertz-Makeham age pattern, a random walk with drift for the period index, and a population with cohort-size waves. Deaths are Poisson draws. By default deaths are reported in 5-year age groups with an open 90+ interval and exposures in single years of age with an open 100+ interval, as in many official statistics.

Usage

mt_example(
  years = 1990:2019,
  deaths = c("grouped", "single"),
  size = 1e+05,
  seed = 1
)

Arguments

years

Calendar years.

deaths

"grouped" (5-year groups and 90+) or "single" (single ages and 100+).

size

Population size at age 30 per year and stratum.

seed

Random seed.

Value

An mt_data object with attribute "truth".

Details

The true rates on the default grid are attached as attribute "truth" (array [age, period, stratum]), which makes the dataset suitable for testing ungrouping and forecast calibration.

Examples

x <- mt_example()
x
#> <mt_data> 2 strata by sex, omega = 110
#>   deaths     5-year groups 30-89, 90+; periods 1990-2019 (width 1); 780 cells
#>   exposure   single years 30-99, 100+; periods 1990-2019 (width 1); 4260 cells
#>   grid       <mt_axis: age, 71 intervals> 30 31 32 33 ... 98 99 100+
#>              <mt_axis: period, 30 intervals> 1990 1991 1992 1993 ... 2017 2018 2019
dim(attr(x, "truth"))
#> [1] 71 30  2
